environment: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300 x64, MSVC 14.51.36231 (Visual Studio 18 Community), CMake 4.4.4, loopback 127.0.0.1
game_exe_sha256: N/A (prototype does not touch the game)
errors: Run 1 (before fixes): client1 Disconnect lost. Run 2: see EXP-006.
objective: End-to-end run of the real executables: one mordor-host and two mordor-client processes on 127.0.0.1 with 40 ms latency, 20 ms jitter and 10% loss on every sender.
hypothesis: Both clients join, receive each other's entity, stay connected and leave cleanly.
expected_result: Exit codes 0; host log shows two player_joined and two player_left; zero invalid packets.
observed_result: Final run passed: both players joined, both left with reason ClientQuit, invalid=0, clients reported 1 remote entity, 0 stale snapshots, 0 prediction corrections. Measured RTT was about 140 ms against about 100 ms of configured delay; the extra is attributed to the 1 ms Sleep main loop (Windows timer granularity), not yet measured separately. Two earlier runs exposed bugs that were then fixed: (1) log fields given a const char* printed 'true' (overload resolution picked bool); (2) a single Disconnect packet could be lost at 10% loss, so the host only noticed the departure by timeout. Disconnect notices are now sent 3 times.
follow_up: Use waitable timers or timeBeginPeriod in the executables and measure the RTT overhead.
